title: Steps to Shrink a Binary Number to One
statement:
You get a positive integer written in binary as the string s (no leading zeros). Repeat these steps until the number is 1:

  • if the number is even, divide it by 2;
  • if it is odd, add 1.

Return how many steps it takes. The string can be up to 500 digits long, far beyond any built-in integer type.

examples.why: 7 → 8 → 4 → 2 → 1. Adding 1 to a block of ones turns them all into zeros with one carry, so the halvings that follow cost one step each.

hints: Dividing by 2 drops the last bit. Adding 1 to an odd number changes which bits?
Work from the last bit towards the front, remembering a carry from earlier additions. The current last bit is the original bit plus the carry.

If that effective bit is 1, it costs two steps (add, then halve) and leaves a carry of 1; if it is 0 (or 2, which is 0 with carry), it costs one halving. At the end, a leftover carry adds one more halving at the front.

explain.intuition:
Simulating with big integers works but copies 500 digits per step. Instead, notice that every step only ever looks at the last bit: halving removes it, and adding 1 to an odd number only creates a carry that ripples to the left. So walk the bits from right to left with a carry.

At each position except the first, the effective bit is bit + carry. If it is 1, the number is odd: add 1 (the bit becomes 0 and a carry of 1 moves left) and then halve, two steps. If it is 0 or 2, the number is even and one halving drops it (a 2 keeps carry 1). When you reach the leading 1, a carry of 1 means the number is 10 in binary, which needs one more halving.
steps: For i from the last index down to 1: let b = s[i] + carry.
If b = 1: add 2 to steps and set carry = 1. Otherwise add 1 to steps (the carry stays as it is).
pitfalls: Converting s to a regular number. 500 bits overflows every built-in integer type and loses precision in floating point.
Treating the leading bit like the others. It is not processed in the loop; only a leftover carry costs a final step.
Resetting the carry to 0 when the effective bit is 2. The carry keeps moving left until it lands on a 0.

solutions.title: Simulate with big integers
solutions.idea: Parse the string into an arbitrary-precision integer and follow the rules literally.

solutions.title: Right-to-left with a carry
solutions.idea: Each bit except the first costs one step if it is effectively even and two if it is odd; a final carry costs one more.

followups: Now you may choose to add 1 or subtract 1 for odd numbers. What is the fewest number of steps?
Return the number of steps for every prefix of s. Can you reuse work between prefixes?
lcTitle: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number in Binary Representation to One
